text:
Maya: Heads up — ACME asked for clearer behavior around burst smoothing + SLA handoff for Dedicated pools. They saw tail latency spikes during a recent demo and want launch gates before GA. cc @kevin @sam
Kevin: Understood. Do we have telemetry scoped to their reserved pool? @infra-bot can you pull 7d p95/p99 for dedicated pools and specifically for acme-prod?
infra-bot: Query submitted: /metrics dedicated_pools.latency p95,p99 7d filter(pool=\"acme-prod\") — preliminary results: p95≈120ms, p99≈420ms during burst windows (spikes aligned with ingress surge).
Sam: 420ms p99 is rough. Is that concentrated on a few heavy tenants or across the pool? We need per-tenant tail to decide preempt vs smoothing.
Maya: ACME provided context: their traffic pattern is sustained 80% baseline with 20–40s spikes at ~3x. They want no user-visible errors during those spikes but are okay with slightly higher latency if capped.
Jess: Proposal: introduce a 30s "degradation window" where we allow higher latency but avoid hard evictions. Implement soft-spill to fallback (cheaper model or queued responses) and a burst-smoothing token bucket. Launch criteria: in canary region, p99 <= 300ms for 48h with the soft-spill enabled.
Kevin: Implementation notes: autoscale cooldown=60s, token-bucket smoothing with refill_rate=5 qps and bucket_size=300. Config-ish: `burst_smoothing: { bucket_size: 300, refill_qps: 5 }`. This prevents immediate saturations but gives limited burst allowance.
Sam: Concern: token-bucket + cooldown could increase preemption pressure for shared pools. For reserved pools we should prefer soft-lease semantics and spillover priority rather than evicting other reserved customers.
Maya: ACME's legal wants explicit SLA text: no hard evictions during business hours, plus defined failure modes for graceful degradation. We should draft SLA wording that matches the soft-spill behavior.
Jess: Ops runbook changes: add a "burst handoff" checklist — steps to flip on soft-spill, monitor p99, roll back if sustained p99>400ms for >15min. Also add tracing tag `burst_handled=true` for debug.
Maya: Action items: 1) Kevin to run load sims w/ proposed bucket settings and post results here. 2) Sam to draft SLA/contract wording for soft-spill + business-hours clause. 3) Jess to write runbook checklist and canary gating steps. 4) Maya to communicate proposed launch gates to ACME and get buy-in. Deadline: EOD Wed.
Kevin: Will run sims and include per-tenant tail breakdown. Posting rough sim plan: 72h replay using acme-prod traffic heatmap, inject 30s 3x bursts every 10m, measure p95/p99 and error rate.
(24h later)
Kevin: sim finished — with bucket_size=300 & refill_qps=5 and autoscale cooldown 60s, canary region p99 reduced to ~290ms for acme-prod across the 72h test. We still see micro-spikes near session churns; overall error rate stayed <0.01%. Results + plots: https://redwood.internal/sims/1765554321 (link) :charts: 
Maya: Thanks. Can we tighten gate to p99<280ms for GA? ACME would prefer tighter numbers but accepts soft-spill if we can guarantee no hard evictions for 72h in primary region.
Sam: I can update preempt policy: soft-lease + spillover priority + preemption credits. Also will add a config flag `reserve_policy: { hard_evictions: false_during_business_hours: true }` and document fallback precedence.
Jess: I'll add the canary gating steps: must pass p99<280ms & error_rate<0.02% for 72h in canary before staged rollout. Also will include rollback criteria.
Maya: Cool — next steps captured. :thumbsup:
Kevin: Posting sim artifacts and will schedule a quick sync with ACME ops after Sam finalizes SLA wording.
Sam: Draft SLA posted to drive, pinged legal. I'll bring language back here once reviewed.
Maya: Thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source for launch decisions and action items.
